analysis.title: Middle East Daily
key_insights: Brent futures are trading below USD 115/b and WTI near USD 101/b, both down about 2% since the start of the week, after Brent rose to nearly USD 118/b at the end of last week.
President Trump gave no clear indication of backing a new offensive against Iran over the weekend. He said it would be 'very easy' to 'finish off' Iran but that he would also consider a deal.

Oil time spreads remain well supported, particularly the prompt spread that straddles the period after the early-November US midterm elections, after which a renewed US strike on Iran appears widely expected.

Gold is stabilizing around USD 4,020/oz after falling more than 4% last week, its largest weekly loss since June. The next catalyst is the FOMC decision this week and whether the Fed turns more overtly hawkish.
Markets price the October 28 FOMC decision as essentially no change, while the December meeting has about 21bps of hikes priced in.
Gold may also be hit by selling in risk assets as investors reduce AI-linked equity positions.

In Gulf credit, the KSA complex continues to underperform, closing +2/3bp on 23 October. ADGB closed -2/3bp, and Bahrain bonds closed up to 1.5pt higher, with front-end bonds 35bp tighter and long-end bonds 20bp tighter.
The new MASDAR 31s were well received, closing 99.625/99.875 (-3bp) from a 99.437 reoffer.
The credit trader notes that risk markets are on edge, with oil up, credit indices wider, tech spreads widening (SPCX) and equities wobbling.

GCC hiring rose 2% in Q3 2026 after a 3% contraction in Q2 (Cooper Fitch Gulf Employment Index). The UAE led with +4%, Saudi Arabia rose 1.5% and Oman 0.5%, while Qatar (-1%), Kuwait (-2%) and Bahrain (-2%) contracted.
By sector, GCC energy hiring rose 7% and strategy and senior finance roles rose 6% each. Banking hiring fell 4% and investment management hiring fell 5%.
The AfDB approved USD 487m for the third phase of Morocco's economic governance and climate resilience support programme.
